raw_response:
I am not going to spread too much this year. My land is only 3.5 mu, and cash has to last the whole season. On my better 2.5 mu I will keep the usual wheat-maize rotation, because that is the safest way for my family: wheat gives steady grain, and maize after wheat brings the second income. I will leave 1 mu for cotton, because cotton still brings cash if the price is decent, and some people around me still plant it. I did not go to much school, so I mostly follow what has worked on my own land and what the neighbors do. If I cut fertilizer too much and the crop turns yellow, the loss is bigger than the money I save, so I will still put enough on. But I also cannot spend like a big farm, so I use round amounts and split it where it matters most.

For wheat, I will sow in early October like usual, use a common improved local variety, put most fertilizer before sowing and a smaller topdress at jointing. I have well water, so if the winter and spring are dry I will irrigate about three times. After wheat harvest in June, I will plant summer maize quickly on the same land, with little tillage because the turnaround is tight and I cannot lose time. For cotton on the 1 mu, I will plant in mid to late April, use a hybrid seed if I can get it locally, and manage it a bit more carefully for insects because cotton is troublesome if pests get ahead. Most work will still be family labor.
